subject.title: feat(googlechat): support Application Default Credentials for outbound auth

question: Should `channels.googlechat.serviceAccountAdc` promise standard Google Application Default Credentials across supported ADC sources, or be deliberately scoped and named as guarded GCE metadata-service-account authentication?
rationale: The current public wording promises ADC and names workload identity, but the final code bypasses Google Auth discovery and directly targets the Compute metadata endpoint; choosing the supported deployment contract is a maintainer product and compatibility decision.

options.title: Implement full guarded ADC support
options.body: Preserve the generic ADC name by supporting the standard credential-discovery sources through an equally controlled network boundary, then prove at least one non-metadata source.

options.title: Scope to GCE metadata identity
options.body: Rename and document the option as a guarded GCE metadata-service-account mode, remove broader ADC/workload-identity claims, and retain the narrow static endpoint design.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Leave existing explicit service-account credentials as the sole supported outbound path until a maintainer-approved ADC boundary design exists.

recommendation.title: Implement full guarded ADC support
recommendation.body: Preserve the generic ADC name by supporting the standard credential-discovery sources through an equally controlled network boundary, then prove at least one non-metadata source.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing PR discussion explicitly routes the metadata and security-boundary decision to this person.
